A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Sections 1–7, Figure 1, and Appendices A–D can be matched reliably; the changed formatting introduces no material comparison gaps.

before.justification: Figure 1 in v1 reports original synthetic logistic-regression results: training and test logistic risk and zero-one error along the GD trajectory.

after.justification: Figure 1 in v2 retains these original simulation results. Their retention from v1 still qualifies as original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: The logistic objective, zero-initialized fixed-step GD update, oracle stopping criteria, and comparison with ℓ2-regularized ERM are unchanged. Added stopping-time and loss-function remarks do not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic binary logistic-regression setting in Figure 1. No dataset, domain, or evaluated scenario is added; discussion of other loss functions does not constitute additional evaluation.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the same GD trajectories and Bayes-risk references. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed; the new related-work citations are not experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Figure 1 retains d = 2000, n = 1000, covariance eigenvalues i^-2, the same signal specification, logistic-risk and zero-one-error metrics, and optimization length eta*t. No evaluation protocol is revised or added.

E4.justification: The same GD-path illustration is retained without additional ablations, robustness tests, or empirical analyses. Appendices A–D remain theoretical proofs; the expanded mechanism discussion adds no experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports simulation seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The theoretical probability bounds are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Both panels of Figure 1 reuse identical plot content, including training/test trajectories, Bayes-risk lines, and insets. No empirical result entries or findings are added, removed, or revised.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, bounds, counterexample, and proofs in Appendices A–D retain their substance. Renaming the positive-dual support set from S to S+ and moving the monotonic-risk observation outside Theorem 3.1 are presentational. The added stopping-time and conjecture discussion supplies explanation rather than a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: calibration through early stopping, polynomial versus exponential sample-complexity separation, and norm/angular connections with ℓ2 regularization.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of learned versus ignored dimensions in Section 3.1 and the uninformative-dimension mechanism behind Theorem 4.2. Section 5.2 expands the geometric rationale for the existing conjecture and explicitly states that current bounds cannot determine whether early stopping or ℓ2 regularization achieves better risk rates. Section 3.1 also notes applicability to other convex, smooth, Lipschitz losses.

D1.justification: The simulation specifications and GD initialization/update information are unchanged. v2 adds no implementation settings, hardware or runtime information, or code/data access instructions; its stopping-time discussion remains conceptual.

R1.justification: v2 adds Sonthalia et al. (2024), Sur and Candès (2019), and Candès and Sur (2020). Section 6 adds a limited comparison with proportional-limit research on logistic ERM existence, while retaining the paper's broader positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds explanatory paragraphs in Sections 3–6 and a generic Impact Statement, revises the Section 5 introduction, and changes the author contribution footnote and support-set notation. Most prose and the section/appendix sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes an ICML-format document with two-column main text and references, revised title/author formatting, running headers, typography, and extensively reflowed equations. Figure 1 moves from the introduction to the preliminaries while preserving its panels and data. The appendices remain single-column but are also reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 improves interpretability through explanations of the lower-bound mechanism and geometric conjecture, and clarifies that the current bounds cannot settle the risk-rate comparison with ℓ2 regularization. The added related-work distinctions also help readers assess scope. These are useful but limited gains: the formal results, appendix proofs, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
